records.subagent_summary: Execution 148.196 scored 0 of 8: four rollouts hit the 16384-token cap and all four finishers collapsed each reading of the public value first, then argued a speaker who knows their own number can compute the partner directly, called both readings contradictory, and boxed the same wrong value. Across rounds 3, 5 and 9 no rollout has ever executed the incumbent's 'group candidates by the value that speaker privately knows' step, because that phrasing does not say what a group contains. This edit replaces the inert grouping clause with the same test stated as an executable count over the written list - how many candidates a speaker cannot tell apart, given only the public value plus their own private one - which mechanically keeps candidates from different readings in one count. It is one token shorter than the incumbent, and counting indistinguishable cases transfers to any knowledge-announcement problem.

Fresh rollouts (148.197) scored 7/8; the single miss again derived the correct locus quadratic, then spent a 16384-token budget calling the unnormalized form an ellipse 55 times and hit the length cap. Clause-tracing all eight traces shows 'check exceptional values' is inert (0/8 mention any exceptional value) while completing the square is what every trace actually does (8/8, 1-7 times each) to turn its x,y equation into center-radius form. This edit therefore swaps only that one dead clause for the move the rollouts rely on, at the identical 70 tokens, keeping the w=(z-1)/z anchor (round 6 lost by generalizing it) and the geometric-or-xy fork (round 7 lost by replacing it), and appending no guard (rounds 2 and 4 lost that way).

Rollouts scored 4/8. One never closed the reasoning block; two closed at 96-98 percent of budget and were truncated part-way through a long recap before reaching any box, and one asserted the small figure lay wholly inside the large one and boxed the containment value. So all three of this hint's clause families (close-early, box-first, coordinates-and-extent) are still the right targets. But rounds 6-9 tried replacing or deleting each of them in turn and every attempt lost held-out (0.225 down to 0.1375-0.1875), so no clause here is safely removable or improvable by rewording. The one untested move is a strictly meaning-preserving compression: same eight instructions in the same order, no step weakened, 161 Qwen tokens against the incumbent's 169. That cuts the transfer tax on ten unseen problems and wins the length tiebreak.

Fresh round-10 rollouts (148.199) scored 5/8. All three failures repeat the one jam this hint has fought for six rounds: they insist a high-degree polynomial must be affine on its own block, then report a single factor (the menu size, or a per-block cap of 4, or degree-plus-one from differencing the whole sequence). Rounds 5, 6 and 7 each added a dedicated clause against exactly that jam and held-out fell every time (0.225 -> 0.1625, 0.15, 0.15), so I did not attack it again. This is instead a strictly lossless compression: 145 vs 153 tokens with every step preserved (differencing ban, index=input, shared affine target, grouping, deg-P root cap, the one-more-forces-P=L tightening, sum-across-the-menu total, block construction). Fewer tokens of identical strategy should transfer at least as well and wins the length tiebreak.

Seven of eight rollouts were correct and none ran out of budget. The sole failure pinned the constants correctly, derived the right single-variable equation and the right root, then evaluated the defining relation at that root with a flipped sign and built the last vertex by pure vector arithmetic, never putting either derived point back through the defining equation; it boxed the resulting wrong area. Round 9's instructive failure broke the same way, so this is a twice-observed systematic weakness. The incumbent's unattached "then verify" sits on the constants, which all eight rollouts got right, so it is inert there; those exact tokens are moved into the operative step to name what actually needs checking - the defining equation must hold at every point, derived ones included. All other clauses, including relabel, are kept verbatim, and length is exactly at incumbent parity, 70 tokens.

Fresh rollouts scored 2/8 and the split is clean: both rewarded runs priced the event by writing a run of moves, noticing most moves were forced, counting only the genuinely free binary choices, and taking one half to that count. The six failures never priced a run at all: four substituted a uniform guess (1/24, 1/16, 1/4, 1/2) and two thrashed over reachability until the token limit. A clause grep of all eight shows labeling, forced-move, arrived-first and one-half language present 6-8/8 while 'sum to one', 'red flag' and 'unreachable' appear 1/8, so no clause was cut. The edit changes only the closing directive: the incumbent's abstract 'multiply true per-step probabilities along each admissible word' becomes the concrete move the winners found unaided - write the run, mark each move forced or free, count the free ones, chance is one half to that power - at 176 tokens vs 177.

Fresh round-10 rollouts scored 1/8 and seven emitted no boxed value at all. The failure is not reaching the rule but refusing to accept it: the closest loser derived the correct signed rule from two exact small cases, then burned its remaining budget asking how to derive it ('but how' 30 times, 'must be a mistake' 5 times) and hit the cap; three others computed a correct small-case value, found a half-built theory disagreeing, declared their own arithmetic mistaken, and abandoned the table. The lone winner was the only rollout that accepted its two-size pattern and stopped. The incumbent's closing 'Confirm on one more size, then commit' feeds this: no rollout ever attempts a fourth size, and 'commit' is too vague to license stopping. I keep every clause the winner used verbatim and swap only that closing for an explicit sufficiency-plus-stop rule, at the same 70 tokens.

Fresh round-10 rollouts scored 7/8. All eight ran the gcd/divisor machinery and the lone failure was again a selection pick among candidates it had already listed - a fork I tried to patch in rounds 2, 4, 6 and 7 and lost held-out every time, so I left it alone. New evidence: every one of the eight summed the stage totals numerically in its opening paragraph and none introduced a symbol before arithmetic, so 'substitute numbers only at the end' is text the student never executes. This is a single-clause deletion of that inert phrase with every load-bearing move kept verbatim: no rule, prohibition, tiebreak or paraphrase added. 116 tokens versus 123, and my only two wins for this hint (rounds 3 and 5) were evidence-backed deletions.

0/8 this round: every rollout hit the 16384-token cap with nothing boxed. All eight adopted the symmetry ansatz, so that part works, but the incumbent's 'read the requested outputs straight from the symmetry relation' says what to achieve without naming any operation, so each fell back to solving for the cubic's coefficients, produced fractional or contradictory ones, and looped ('contradiction' 1-21 times per rollout, two concluding no such polynomials exist). This replaces that inert directive with the three concrete evaluation moves the relation actually supplies - reflect an unknown argument onto a known one, swap maps via q = s - p, and use the center as a fixed point - so values are obtainable with no coefficients at all. These moves are generic to any point-symmetry functional equation, and it is shorter than the incumbent (148 vs 152 tokens).

Six of eight rollouts (1/8 correct) hit the 16384-token cap: after measuring only the single smallest case they jumped to an open-ended symbolic composite-permutation argument and spent thousands of tokens re-litigating their own contradictory cycle bookkeeping, never boxing anything; the one success simply measured two sizes and generalized. The incumbent's 'convention slipped' sentence appears in none of the eight traces, and 'get one more size the same way' is too vague to hold them there, so both are replaced by one concrete, countable gate - three measured rows in a parameter-versus-count table before any general argument, then one formula checked against every row. This is shorter than the incumbent and should transfer to any 'in terms of n' question by forcing data collection to finish before abstraction starts.
